transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, to be perfectly honest, ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself. I find myself crying over little things, like the church potluck lists, and I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle easy. I've even started missing church planning things that I never, ever would have missed before. It's just... I'm having a really hard time keeping up with it all lately.
When exactly did your friend pass away, and when did you first start noticing these changes in yourself?

She passed away just about a month ago. It was very sudden. And... well, it was only after losing her that I really started falling apart with all the church planning. I didn't have any trouble keeping up before that, it all just started right after she died.

Besides missing your friend and the church activities, have you noticed that other things you normally enjoy—like hobbies, time with family, or activities outside of church—have stopped feeling enjoyable or interesting to you?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still like spending time with my family, and... well, my regular things around the house are fine. I haven't really lost interest in them. It's really just the church things that are feeling so hard right now, and the crying. But my family time is still perfectly fine.

Apart from the crying and difficulty with church activities, how has your overall mood been? Do you find yourself feeling persistently sad or down most of the day, or is it more that you just feel overwhelmed when thinking about your friend or the church responsibilities?

I wouldn't say I feel sad all day long, no. It's really just when I think about her, or when I look at the church schedule and see everything I'm supposed to be doing. That's when I get overwhelmed and start crying. The rest of the time, my mood is mostly okay.

On days when you're not thinking about your friend or looking at the church schedule, would you say your mood feels basically normal, or do you still feel sad or down even when you're not actively thinking about these things?

I would say it feels basically normal. If I'm just... going about my day and not focused on those things, I feel fine. I don't just sit around feeling down for no reason. It really is just tied to her passing and all the church stuff I'm behind on.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels since your friend passed away—or do those things feel pretty much the same as they were before?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. I'm sleeping about the same as I always do, and I'm eating normally. My energy is fine, too, as long as I'm not getting overwhelmed by the church stuff. So, yeah, all of that feels pretty much the same as before.
